minutes.headline: Water commissioners reviewed a draft RFP to re-bid the water tank cell antenna lease after T-Mobile's contract expired.
minutes.summary: The commission went through the attorney's draft RFP for cellular carriers on the water tank, settling terms such as building size, antenna limits, the escalator and the proposal deposit. It also heard that the three-year copper and lead tests passed, discussed renting equipment to clear the site, and planned timing for a special district election.

budget_items.what_was_said: Draft RFP sets a minimum annual payment close to what T-Mobile pays now; AT&T pays more.
A three percent annual escalator is kept, lower than the previous contract's.
The draft has a deposit for bidders; members did not favour charging one and left it to the attorney.
Insurance only needs the replacement value of rented equipment to issue a binder.

decisions.decision: Equipment building size limit to be raised, about 300 square feet, or sized to the biggest existing building.
Antenna limit set at 12 per carrier, not 12 total.
Draft RFP goes back to the attorneys to tighten, then is issued publicly, with tank maintenance and equipment-move language emphasised.
Superintendent may rent equipment to clear the site.
Special election polls open 4 to 6 on the 17th, with the regular meeting at 5:30 and the special meeting opened at six.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners worked through the attorney's draft RFP to re-bid the cell antenna lease on the water tank after T-Mobile's contract expired, with no vote taken.
They set the equipment building limit to rise to about 300 square feet or the largest existing building, and limited antennas to 12 per carrier.
The draft keeps an annual escalator below the previous contract's and a minimum payment near the current rent; members did not favour a bidder deposit and left it to the attorney.
The draft goes back to the attorneys to tighten, then is issued publicly, with tank maintenance and equipment-move language emphasised.
The commission heard the three-year copper and lead tests passed, agreed the superintendent may rent equipment to clear the site, and planned a special election on the 17th.

why_it_matters: The tank's cell lease is revenue for the water district, and the terms of the new RFP (minimum payment, escalator, number of antennas) set what carriers pay and how much of the site they take for years.
The passed copper and lead tests are a result a water customer can rely on, and the special election is a vote residents of the district will be asked to take.
